title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第4部分：运动中的随机

chapters.Likelihood: 2. 拟合钟形曲线：最大似然
chapters.MCMC: 7. 从无法直接采样的分布中采样
chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现

32eff79146fc.en: Here are six hundred dots, scattered completely at random. <bookmark mark='a'/> Now let each one wander. At every moment it gets a small random kick, plus a gentle push from a field of arrows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watch what the randomness builds.
32eff79146fc.zh: 这里有600个点，完全随机地散布着。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在，让每个点随意游荡。每一刻，它都会被随机地轻踢一下，同时还被一片箭头场轻轻推一把。<bookmark mark='b'/>看看随机性会搭出什么来。

0ebc69b6ea13.en: This is, in miniature, how today's image and video generators work. They start from noise and let it flow, one random step at a time, into a picture. <bookmark mark='a'/> The arrows are the whole secret: they're what a network learns. We'll build them in part fourteen.
0ebc69b6ea13.zh: 这就是当今图像和视频生成器工作方式的缩影。它们从噪声出发，让它一次一小步、随机地流动，最后变成一幅画面。<bookmark mark='a'/>那些箭头就是全部的秘密：网络要学的，正是它们。我们会在第14部分把它们搭出来。

a3081902426a.en: Run it the other way, with the arrows gone, and the letters dissolve back into noise. <bookmark mark='a'/> Both directions are random motion, and the same mathematics describes them.
a3081902426a.zh: 反过来运行，去掉箭头，这些字母又溶解回噪声。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个方向都是随机运动，描述它们的，是同一套数学。

563969b05dc7.en: So this part is about randomness: how to describe it, how to learn from it, how to draw samples from it, and how it moves. <bookmark mark='a'/> It's the last piece of mathematics we need before the models themselves.
563969b05dc7.zh: 所以，这一部分讲的是随机性：怎样描述它，怎样从中学习，怎样从中抽取样本，以及它怎样运动。<bookmark mark='a'/>在进入模型本身之前，这是我们需要的最后一块数学。

3d0cec005e58.en: Drop a ball through twelve rows of pegs. At every peg it bounces left or right, fifty-fifty. <bookmark mark='a'/> Where it lands just counts its right bounces. <bookmark mark='b'/> One ball tells you nothing. Eighty start to show a shape.
3d0cec005e58.zh: 让一个小球穿过12排钉子落下。每碰到一颗钉子，它就向左或向右弹开，机会各占一半。<bookmark mark='a'/>它最后落在哪里，只取决于它向右弹了几次。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个球，什么也说明不了。80个球，就开始显出一个形状了。

f1903e25e4c9.en: A thousand make it unmistakable. <bookmark mark='a'/> Counting paths gives the exact chances: twelve choose k, the number of paths with k right bounces, out of two to the twelve paths in all. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the smooth curve hugging them is the bell: the normal distribution, with a centre mu and a width sigma. Here the centre is six, and the width is the square root of three. Galton built this board in the 1870s to show it, but de Moivre had found the curve in 1733.
f1903e25e4c9.zh: 到了1000个球，这个形状就确定无疑了。<bookmark mark='a'/>数一数路径，就能得到精确的概率：12选k，也就是向右弹k次的路径数，除以全部路径数，2的12次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>而紧贴着它们的那条光滑曲线，就是钟形曲线：正态分布，它有一个中心μ和一个宽度σ。这里中心是6，宽度是根号3。19世纪70年代，弗朗西斯·高尔顿造了这块板子来演示它，不过早在1733年，棣莫弗就已经发现了这条曲线。

28d73fa50f58.en: But why a bell, and why so often? Take one die: six flat bars. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add two dice, and you get a triangle. Three, and it's already rounding off. <bookmark mark='b'/> Six. Twelve. The bell again. <bookmark mark='c'/> That's the central limit theorem. Add up many independent random pieces, and whatever shape the pieces have, the sum takes the shape of the bell, <bookmark mark='d'/> with a spread that grows like the square root of how many you add. Errors, heights, noise: anything built from many small independent nudges comes out bell-shaped.
28d73fa50f58.zh: 可为什么偏偏是钟形，又为什么这么常见？拿一个骰子：6根一样高的柱子。<bookmark mark='a'/>把两个骰子的点数加起来，得到一个三角形。三个，形状已经开始变圆了。<bookmark mark='b'/>6个。12个。又是钟形曲线。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是中心极限定理。把许多独立的随机小块加起来，不管每一块是什么形状，总和都会变成钟形，<bookmark mark='d'/>而它的散布程度，按加进去的个数的平方根增长。误差、身高、噪声：凡是由许多微小而独立的推动累积起来的东西，最后都是钟形的。

205682a496c4.en: Chapter two. Fitting a bell to data.
205682a496c4.zh: 第2章。用钟形曲线拟合数据。

0ebfe3cf60c2.en: Here are the thousand balls again. Which bell describes them best? <bookmark mark='a'/> Try one. Score it like this: at each ball, read off the bell's height, take the log, and average over all the balls. That's the log-likelihood: how well this bell predicted where the balls actually went. <bookmark mark='b'/> A bell in the wrong place scores badly. <bookmark mark='c'/> So does one that's too narrow, <bookmark mark='d'/> or too wide. <bookmark mark='e'/> The best bell, the maximum likelihood fit, is the one under which the data was least surprising.
0ebfe3cf60c2.zh: 还是那1000个球。哪条钟形曲线最能描述它们？<bookmark mark='a'/>先试一条。这样给它打分：在每个球的位置，读出钟形曲线的高度，取对数，再对所有球求平均。这就是对数似然：这条钟形曲线，把球的实际落点预测得有多好。<bookmark mark='b'/>位置放错的钟形曲线，得分很低。<bookmark mark='c'/>太窄的也一样，<bookmark mark='d'/>太宽的也一样。<bookmark mark='e'/>最好的那一条，也就是最大似然拟合，是让数据显得最不意外的那一条。

3fe0a32b1dda.en: Score every possible bell, every centre and every width, and the scores form a landscape. <bookmark mark='a'/> From part three, we know how to find its top: follow the gradient uphill. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the summit, the centre is the balls' average, 5.96, and the width is their spread, 1.71, close to the square root of three that the pegs predict. For a bell, maximum likelihood comes out as the two most natural summaries of the data.
3fe0a32b1dda.zh: 给每一条可能的钟形曲线打分，遍历每个中心、每个宽度，这些得分就构成一片地形。<bookmark mark='a'/>第3部分讲过怎样找到它的顶峰：沿着梯度往上爬。<bookmark mark='b'/>到了山顶，中心就是这些球的平均值，5.96，宽度就是它们的离散程度，1.71，接近钉子所预言的根号3。对钟形曲线来说，最大似然给出的，正是对数据最自然的两个概括。

1bc10ca3fb70.en: And here's the connection to everything else. Maximizing the average log-likelihood <bookmark mark='a'/> is the same as minimizing the average surprise, <bookmark mark='b'/> and that's part one's cross-entropy, measured against the data. <bookmark mark='c'/> Maximum likelihood is minimum cross-entropy. It's how every model in this series is trained, from a bell curve to a language model.
1bc10ca3fb70.zh: 这就是它和其他一切的联系。最大化平均对数似然，<bookmark mark='a'/>等于最小化平均意外度，<bookmark mark='b'/>而这就是第1部分的交叉熵，对照数据来计算。<bookmark mark='c'/>最大似然就是最小交叉熵。本系列的每一个模型，从一条钟形曲线到一个语言模型，都是这样训练的。

8e4cb6b6828e.en: Chapter three. Belief as a distribution.

d267e7fb7895.en: How often is a letter an e? Before reading anything, we have no idea: any fraction from zero to one seems as plausible as any other. That's a belief, and we can draw it, as a flat line over every possibility. <bookmark mark='a'/> Bayes's rule says how to update a belief when evidence arrives. Multiply what you believed by how well each possibility explains the evidence, then rescale, so the total is one again.
d267e7fb7895.zh: 一个字母是e的频率有多高？在读任何东西之前，我们毫无头绪：从0到1之间的任何比例，看起来都同样可信。这就是一种信念，我们可以把它画出来：横跨所有可能性的一条平线。<bookmark mark='a'/>贝叶斯法则告诉我们，证据到来时，该怎样更新信念。把你原来的信念，乘以每种可能对证据解释得有多好，再重新缩放，让总和重新等于1。

8c1bc93289c8.en: Read the first ten letters: three e's. <bookmark mark='a'/> The belief leans toward a third, but it's still wide. <bookmark mark='b'/> After a hundred letters, it's narrower. <bookmark mark='c'/> After a thousand, narrower still. <bookmark mark='d'/> After ten thousand, it's a sharp peak near 0.127: ninety-five percent of the belief lies between 0.120 and 0.134. <bookmark mark='e'/> The whole passage, all sixteen thousand letters, gives 0.122, inside that range.
8c1bc93289c8.zh: 读前10个字母：有3个e。<bookmark mark='a'/>信念偏向三分之一，但仍然很宽。<bookmark mark='b'/>读了100个字母之后，它变窄了。<bookmark mark='c'/>1000个之后，更窄。<bookmark mark='d'/>1万个之后，它成了0.127附近的一个尖峰：95%的信念落在0.120到0.134之间。<bookmark mark='e'/>整个段落，全部16000个字母，给出0.122，正在这个范围之内。

c7bfab09bf23.en: So the answer isn't one number. It's a distribution: a best guess with its uncertainty attached, narrowing like one over the square root of the evidence. <bookmark mark='a'/> Laplace worked this out in 1774. His best guess after k e's in n letters is k plus one, over n plus two. Before any evidence, that's one half.
c7bfab09bf23.zh: 所以答案不是一个数，而是一个分布：一个最佳猜测，附带着它的不确定性；证据越多，它越窄，宽度与证据量的平方根成反比。<bookmark mark='a'/>拉普拉斯在1774年就算出了这一点。在n个字母里看到k个e之后，他的最佳猜测是n加2分之k加1。在没有任何证据之前，这个值是二分之一。

6986c22dfd82.en: A model never hands us a letter or a word. It hands us a distribution, and to write anything we have to roll the dice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's how a computer rolls loaded dice. Lay the probabilities end to end, from zero to one, so each letter owns a stretch exactly as long as its probability. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pick a uniformly random point, and take the letter it lands in. Each letter wins exactly as often as its probability says. <bookmark mark='c'/> These letters are drawn from part one's letter frequencies.
6986c22dfd82.zh: 模型从来不会直接交给我们一个字母或一个词。它交给我们的是一个分布，要写出任何东西，我们都得掷骰子。<bookmark mark='a'/>计算机是这样掷灌铅骰子的。把各个概率首尾相接，从0排到1，让每个字母占据一段，长度正好等于它的概率。<bookmark mark='b'/>均匀随机地取一个点，看它落在哪个字母那一段里。每个字母被选中的频率，正好等于它的概率。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些字母，是按第1部分的字母频率抽出来的。

57747f3085c8.en: Language models do the same with words, with one dial added. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's GPT-2's distribution for the word after: Spade sat down in the armchair, and. Its favourite, I, gets only four percent; the other fifty thousand words share the rest. <bookmark mark='b'/> The dial is the temperature: divide the scores by T before the softmax.
57747f3085c8.zh: 语言模型对词也做同样的事，只是多了一个旋钮。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是GPT-2给出的下一个词的分布，前文是：“斯佩德在扶手椅上坐下，然后”。它最看好的词是I，也就是“我”，却只得到4%；其余大约5万个词，分掉剩下的部分。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个旋钮就是温度：在softmax之前，先把分数除以T。

7f59cb437f95.en: Turn it down, below one, and the distribution sharpens toward the favourites. <bookmark mark='a'/> Turn it up, and it flattens, until any word at all might come next. <bookmark mark='b'/> The entropy, part one's measure of uncertainty, follows the dial: under five bits at a half, nine at one, thirteen and a half at two.
7f59cb437f95.zh: 把温度调低，低于1，分布就向那几个热门词收拢。<bookmark mark='a'/>调高，它就变平，直到任何一个词都可能接在后面。<bookmark mark='b'/>熵，也就是第1部分衡量不确定性的那个量，跟着旋钮变化：温度0.5时不到5比特，1时是9比特，2时是13.5比特。

b5258829e720.en: Here's what comes out, twenty-four words at a time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Always taking the favourite is safe and flat. <bookmark mark='b'/> At a half, still sensible. <bookmark mark='c'/> At one, sampling the model's own distribution, it's stranger and more varied. <bookmark mark='d'/> At two, it falls apart. Choosing how to sample is a real design decision, and we'll come back to it.
b5258829e720.zh: 这是生成出来的结果，每次24个词。<bookmark mark='a'/>总是取最热门的词，稳妥，但平淡。<bookmark mark='b'/>温度0.5，仍然通顺。<bookmark mark='c'/>温度1，也就是按模型自己的分布采样，更古怪，也更多样。<bookmark mark='d'/>温度2，就彻底散架了。怎样采样，是一个实实在在的设计决策，我们以后还会回到这个问题。

305ca0001194.en: A Markov chain is randomness with a short memory: what comes next depends only on where you are now. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's one built from part one's letters, with just three states: a space, a vowel, or a consonant. The arrows carry the chances of what comes next. After a vowel, a consonant, seven times in ten. <bookmark mark='b'/> Follow one walker as it hops, and count the time it spends in each state.
305ca0001194.zh: 马尔可夫链，是一种记性很短的随机性：接下来发生什么，只取决于你现在在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是用第1部分的字母搭成的一条链，只有三个状态：空格、元音，或者辅音。箭头上标着接下来各种情况的概率。元音之后，10次里有7次是辅音。<bookmark mark='b'/>跟着一个行走者，看它跳来跳去，数一数它在每个状态上待了多久。

b59ec342522a.en: Keep going, and the shares settle: about nineteen percent spaces, thirty-one percent vowels, and fifty percent consonants, the same shares as in the books. <bookmark mark='a'/> Markov did exactly this by hand in 1913, with the vowels and consonants of twenty thousand letters of Pushkin.
b59ec342522a.zh: 一直走下去，这些比例就稳定下来：大约19%是空格，31%是元音，50%是辅音，和书里的比例一样。<bookmark mark='a'/>1913年，马尔可夫正是靠手算做了这件事，用的是普希金《叶甫盖尼·奥涅金》里2万个字母的元音和辅音。

9448d7213001.en: Follow the whole distribution instead of a single walker, and each step is a multiplication by the table of chances, the transition matrix. <bookmark mark='a'/> The distribution that a step leaves unchanged is the chain's stationary distribution. It's an eigenvector of the matrix, with eigenvalue one, straight out of part two.
9448d7213001.zh: 不跟单个行走者，而是跟踪整个分布，那么每走一步，就是乘一次那张概率表，也就是转移矩阵。<bookmark mark='a'/>走一步之后保持不变的那个分布，就是这条链的平稳分布。它是这个矩阵的一个特征向量，特征值为1，直接来自第2部分。

0c8cf91b203e.en: Now all twenty-seven letters, with part one's full table. Start from certainty: the letter q. <bookmark mark='a'/> One step later, it's almost surely a u. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the possibilities spread out, <bookmark mark='c'/> and within about five steps the chain has forgotten where it started: what's left is just the letter frequencies. <bookmark mark='d'/> How fast it forgets is set by the matrix's second-largest eigenvalue, about 0.3 here: each step shrinks the distance that's left by roughly that factor.
0c8cf91b203e.zh: 现在换成全部27个字母，用第1部分的完整表格。从确定无疑开始：字母q。<bookmark mark='a'/>一步之后，几乎肯定是u。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后各种可能散开，<bookmark mark='c'/>大约5步之内，这条链就忘了自己从哪里出发：剩下的只是字母频率。<bookmark mark='d'/>它忘得有多快，由矩阵第二大的特征值决定，这里大约是0.3：每走一步，剩下的差距大约就乘以这个数。

309e315ff88a.en: Here's a strange way to compute pi. Throw darts at a square, completely at random. <bookmark mark='a'/> The share that lands inside the circle is the circle's share of the square's area: pi over four. So four times the fraction inside estimates pi. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watch the estimate as the darts pile up. It lurches around, then homes in.
309e315ff88a.zh: 有一种计算圆周率π的奇怪方法。往一个正方形里扔飞镖，完全随机地扔。<bookmark mark='a'/>落在圆内的比例，就是圆占正方形面积的比例：4分之π。所以，把圆内的比例乘以4，就是对π的估计。<bookmark mark='b'/>随着飞镖越积越多，看看这个估计值。它先是东摇西晃，然后渐渐逼近。

1873cd208dc7.en: After four thousand darts: 3.158. <bookmark mark='a'/> The shaded band is how far off a run like this typically is, and it narrows like one over the square root of the number of darts.
1873cd208dc7.zh: 扔了4000支飞镖之后：3.158。<bookmark mark='a'/>阴影带表示这样一次实验通常会偏差多少，它与飞镖数的平方根成反比地收窄。

395b31f3816f.en: Repeat the experiment many times at each size, and measure the typical error. On log scales, it falls on a straight line with slope minus a half. <bookmark mark='a'/> The error shrinks like one over the square root of the number of samples: every extra digit of accuracy costs a hundred times more samples. <bookmark mark='b'/> That's slow. But the rate doesn't care about dimension: averaging random samples works the same in a million dimensions, where any grid would be hopeless. That's why Monte Carlo, named by Ulam and Metropolis after the casino, is everywhere in machine learning.
395b31f3816f.zh: 在每种规模下把实验重复很多次，测出典型误差。在对数坐标上，它们落在一条斜率为负二分之一的直线上。<bookmark mark='a'/>误差与样本数的平方根成反比：精度每多一位数字，就要多花100倍的样本。<bookmark mark='b'/>这很慢。但这个速度与维数无关：对随机样本求平均，在100万维里也一样管用，而在那里，任何网格都毫无希望。正因为这样，蒙特卡洛方法在机器学习里无处不在；这个名字，是乌拉姆和梅特罗波利斯借那座赌场起的。

69183c97aaa4.en: Monte Carlo has one weakness: rare events. How often does a standard bell curve land above four? Exactly, about three times in a hundred thousand. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw ten thousand samples, and only two land there. The estimate is off by a factor of six.
69183c97aaa4.zh: 蒙特卡洛有一个弱点：罕见事件。一条标准钟形曲线，取值落在4以上的频率有多高？精确地说，大约10万次里有3次。<bookmark mark='a'/>抽1万个样本，只有2个落在那里。估计值差了6倍。

573d04129617.en: The fix is to cheat, and then correct for it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Draw from a different bell, one that lands out there half the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then weight each sample by how much more likely it was under the real distribution than under the one you drew from. <bookmark mark='c'/> Same number of samples, and now the answer is within one percent. This is importance sampling, and it comes back when models learn from samples drawn by an older version of themselves, in reinforcement learning.
573d04129617.zh: 解决办法是：先作弊，再把作弊纠正回来。<bookmark mark='a'/>换一条钟形曲线来抽样，它有一半的时候落在那一带。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后给每个样本加权：它在真实分布下的可能性，是在你抽样所用的分布下的多少倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>样本数一样，现在的答案误差却在1%以内。这就是重要性采样。在强化学习里，当模型用自己旧版本抽出的样本来学习时，它还会再次出现。

fd2e1c0e4d54.en: Chapter seven. Markov chain Monte Carlo.
fd2e1c0e4d54.zh: 第7章。马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛。

633fe3480949.en: Monte Carlo needs samples. But often there's no direct way to draw them. All we can do is evaluate how likely each point is, and often only up to an unknown constant. That's exactly Bayes's rule, where the rescaling is the hard part. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's a density in the plane, with two bumps. In 1953, at Los Alamos, Metropolis and his colleagues found a way to sample anything like it. Take a random walk. <bookmark mark='b'/> Propose a small random step. If it goes uphill, take it. <bookmark mark='c'/> If it goes downhill, take it only sometimes, with probability equal to the ratio of the heights. Otherwise, stay where you are.
633fe3480949.zh: 蒙特卡洛需要样本。但很多时候，没有直接抽取样本的办法。我们能做的，只是算出每个点有多大可能，而且常常还差着一个未知的常数因子。贝叶斯法则正是这样：难的就是重新缩放那一步。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是平面上的一个密度，有两个鼓包。1953年，在洛斯阿拉莫斯，梅特罗波利斯和他的同事找到了一种办法，能对任何这样的分布采样。做一次随机游走。<bookmark mark='b'/>随机地提议迈一小步。如果是上坡，就迈出去。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果是下坡，就只是有时候迈出去，概率等于两处高度之比。否则，就留在原地。

bcf2235a58b4.en: Only the ratio appears, so the unknown constant cancels out. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep walking. The places the walker visits pile up exactly like the density: it's a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is the one we wanted. <bookmark mark='b'/> The left bump holds two thirds of the probability, and the walker spends sixty-five percent of its time there. Markov chain Monte Carlo made Bayesian statistics practical, and it's still how physicists sample molecules.
bcf2235a58b4.zh: 式子里只出现比值，所以那个未知常数就约掉了。<bookmark mark='a'/>一直走下去。行走者到过的地方，堆积起来的样子和这个密度一模一样：它是一条马尔可夫链，而它的平稳分布，正是我们想要的那个分布。<bookmark mark='b'/>左边的鼓包占了三分之二的概率，行走者也有65%的时间待在那里。马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛让贝叶斯统计变得切实可行，物理学家至今仍用它来对分子采样。

24a2578f8654.en: In 1827, the botanist Robert Brown watched pollen in water under a microscope, and saw it jiggle, endlessly, for no visible reason. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's a model: a walk that steps up or down at random. Eight steps. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sixty-four smaller steps. A thousand and twenty-four, smaller still. <bookmark mark='c'/> Shrink each step like one over the square root of their number, so the spread after any time stays the same, and the walks settle into a single random object: Brownian motion. It's continuous everywhere, and so jagged it has no slope anywhere.
24a2578f8654.zh: 1827年，植物学家罗伯特·布朗在显微镜下观察水中的花粉微粒，看到它们不停地抖动，永不停歇，却看不出任何原因。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个模型：随机地向上或向下迈步的游走。走8步。<bookmark mark='b'/>64步，每步更小。1024步，每步还要更小。<bookmark mark='c'/>让每一步的大小与步数的平方根成反比，这样任何时刻的散布程度都保持不变，这些游走就会收敛成一个单一的随机对象：布朗运动。它处处连续，却又曲折得处处没有斜率。

69ad638add1a.en: Now draw sixty of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> At any moment, where they've got to follows a bell curve, centred at zero, with spread the square root of t. <bookmark mark='b'/> Twice the time gives about 1.4 times the spread, not twice. Randomness spreads slowly. It's the central limit theorem again: the position at time t is a sum of many tiny independent kicks. <bookmark mark='c'/> Measured on twenty thousand paths, the variances come out at a quarter, a half, three quarters and one: exactly t.
69ad638add1a.zh: 现在画出60条。<bookmark mark='a'/>在任何时刻，它们走到的位置都服从一条钟形曲线，中心在0，散布程度是根号t。<bookmark mark='b'/>时间加倍，散布只变成大约1.4倍，而不是2倍。随机性扩散得很慢。这又是中心极限定理：t时刻的位置，是许多微小而独立的踢动之和。<bookmark mark='c'/>在2万条路径上测量，方差分别是四分之一、二分之一、四分之三和1：正好就是t。

1d2b676859ed.en: In two dimensions, a cloud of particles released at one point spreads into a widening bell. <bookmark mark='a'/> Follow the density instead of the particles, and it obeys an equation with no randomness in it at all: the heat equation. The jiggling of each particle becomes the smooth spreading of the whole. <bookmark mark='b'/> Einstein worked this out in 1905, and used it to argue that molecules are real. A few years later, Jean Perrin measured the jiggling, and counted them.
1d2b676859ed.zh: 在二维平面上，从一点释放的一团粒子，会扩散成一个越来越宽的钟形。<bookmark mark='a'/>不跟踪粒子，而是跟踪密度，它服从的方程里完全没有随机性：热方程。每个粒子的抖动，变成了整体的平滑扩散。<bookmark mark='b'/>1905年，爱因斯坦算出了这一点，并用它来论证分子真实存在。几年后，让·佩兰测量了这种抖动，数出了分子的数目。

cc00fcde36a3.en: Brownian motion is pure jiggle. Add a push, and you have a stochastic differential equation. At each instant, the change in x is a push, f of x times dt, <bookmark mark='a'/> plus a random kick: g times a small piece of Brownian motion. <bookmark mark='b'/> To simulate one, take small steps: push, then kick, with a kick the size of the square root of the step.
cc00fcde36a3.zh: 布朗运动是纯粹的抖动。加上一股推力，就得到一个随机微分方程。在每一瞬间，x的变化等于一股推力，f(x)乘以dt，<bookmark mark='a'/>再加上一次随机踢动：g乘以一小段布朗运动。<bookmark mark='b'/>要模拟它，就迈小步：先推，再踢，踢动的大小是步长的平方根。

ed8931d469db.en: The simplest interesting one is a spring pulling back toward zero, plus noise. Forty particles start at 2.5. <bookmark mark='a'/> The push pulls them home, the noise keeps them stirred, <bookmark mark='b'/> and they settle into a bell around zero, its width set by the balance between the two. It's called the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and it's the one diffusion models use.
ed8931d469db.zh: 最简单又有意思的一个，是一根把东西拉回0的弹簧，再加上噪声。40个粒子从2.5出发。<bookmark mark='a'/>推力把它们拉回家，噪声让它们不停地翻搅，<bookmark mark='b'/>最后它们稳定成0附近的一个钟形，宽度由两者之间的平衡决定。它叫作奥恩斯坦–乌伦贝克过程，扩散模型用的正是它。

e72193c18219.en: And again, follow the density instead of the particles. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start with data that has two peaks, and let every point drift toward zero and jiggle, the way the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process says. <bookmark mark='b'/> Twenty thousand random particles, and the solution of one deterministic equation, the Fokker–Planck equation, move together. <bookmark mark='c'/> Wait long enough, and every trace of the data is gone: what's left is a plain standard bell. That's exactly what a diffusion model does to its training images.
e72193c18219.zh: 同样，不跟踪粒子，而是跟踪密度。<bookmark mark='a'/>从有两个峰的数据出发，让每个点都按奥恩斯坦–乌伦贝克过程说的那样，向0漂移，同时抖动。<bookmark mark='b'/>2万个随机粒子，和一个确定性方程的解，也就是福克–普朗克方程的解，步调一致地移动。<bookmark mark='c'/>等得足够久，数据的痕迹就全都消失了：剩下的只是一条普通的标准钟形曲线。扩散模型对它的训练图像做的，正是这件事。

9101e1c0a1d0.en: Can the film run backwards, from the bell back to the data? In 1982, Brian Anderson showed that reversed in time, it's another stochastic differential equation, with one extra term: <bookmark mark='a'/> the score, the slope of the log of the density at that moment. <bookmark mark='b'/> The score points uphill, toward where the data is more likely.
9101e1c0a1d0.zh: 这部影片能倒着放吗，从钟形曲线回到数据？1982年，布赖恩·安德森证明了：时间反向之后，它是另一个随机微分方程，只多了一项：<bookmark mark='a'/>分数函数，也就是那一刻密度的对数的斜率。<bookmark mark='b'/>分数函数指向上坡，指向数据更可能出现的地方。

66e78464130d.en: Know the score at every noise level, and you can turn noise into data. <bookmark mark='a'/> It's the field of arrows from the start of this part. <bookmark mark='b'/> There, it was computed exactly from the letters. A diffusion model learns it from millions of images, with a network, and that's part fourteen.
66e78464130d.zh: 知道了每个噪声水平下的分数函数，就能把噪声变成数据。<bookmark mark='a'/>它就是这一部分开头的那片箭头场。<bookmark mark='b'/>在那里，它是直接从那些字母精确算出来的。扩散模型则用一个网络，从数百万张图像中把它学出来，这是第14部分的内容。

6dc8b1bbf04a.en: Let's take stock. Many small random pushes add up to a bell. Fitting a model means maximizing likelihood, which is minimizing cross-entropy. Bayes's rule turns evidence into a sharper belief. Sampling turns a distribution into a choice, with temperature as the dial. Markov chains forget where they started, at a rate set by an eigenvalue. Monte Carlo answers questions with random samples, and Metropolis's walk draws them from shapes we can only evaluate. And random motion, run backwards with the score, turns noise into data.
6dc8b1bbf04a.zh: 我们来盘点一下。许多微小的随机推动，加起来就是一条钟形曲线。拟合一个模型，就是最大化似然，也就是最小化交叉熵。贝叶斯法则把证据变成更集中的信念。采样把一个分布变成一个选择，温度就是那个旋钮。马尔可夫链会忘记自己从哪里出发，忘得多快，由一个特征值决定。蒙特卡洛用随机样本来回答问题，而梅特罗波利斯的游走，能从那些我们只能求值的形状中抽出样本。最后，随机运动借助分数函数倒着运行，就能把噪声变成数据。

bd0e0b64ae5e.en: All of this comes back. Maximum likelihood trains every model from part five on. Bayes and Markov chains return in statistical machine learning, in part six. Sampling and importance weights come back when models reason and act, in parts seventeen to nineteen. And stochastic differential equations describe both noisy gradient descent, in part nine, and diffusion models, in part fourteen.
bd0e0b64ae5e.zh: 这些都会再次出现。从第5部分起，每一个模型都靠最大似然来训练。贝叶斯和马尔可夫链，会在第6部分的统计机器学习里回归。采样和重要性权重，会在模型推理和行动时再次出现，在第17到第19部分。而随机微分方程，既描述带噪声的梯度下降，在第9部分，也描述扩散模型，在第14部分。

cc925828730f.en: Next time, act two begins: learning. We start with the classics: least squares and its geometry, logistic regression, kernels and support vector machines, trees and boosting. <bookmark mark='a'/> They ran machine learning before deep learning, and on tables of data they still often win.
cc925828730f.zh: 下一次，第二幕开始：学习。我们从经典方法讲起：最小二乘法及其几何，逻辑回归，核方法与支持向量机，决策树与提升法。<bookmark mark='a'/>在深度学习之前，机器学习靠的就是它们；而在表格数据上，它们至今仍常常胜出。

fa5977b0acb6.en: Blitzstein and Hwang's Introduction to Probability is a friendly place to start, and MacKay's book has the best chapters on Monte Carlo methods. Thanks for watching, and see you in part five.
fa5977b0acb6.zh: 布利茨斯坦与黄的《概率论导论》是一本亲切的入门书，而麦凯的那本书里，有讲蒙特卡洛方法最好的几章。感谢观看，第5部分见。
